diagnosis.root_cause: The shop-db container (postgres:17-alpine) was stopped at 13:13:21 after a kill and stop request, with a clean shutdown and exit code 0, and nothing restarted it. shop-web can no longer resolve the host 'shop-db' from DATABASE_URL, so /health returns 503 and /api/items returns 500.

evidence.detail: At 13:13:21 events show kill, stop and die for shop-db. shop-web was reported unhealthy at 13:13:50, after the database went down.
shop-db is exited with code 0 and OOMKilled false. Its restart count is 0 and its last two health probes passed before the stop. A stale unhealthy label remains.
shop-db logged a fast shutdown request and then a clean shutdown at 13:13:21. This was an external stop, not a crash.
shop-web served 200s until 13:13:30. After that its database health check fails to resolve host 'shop-db', which is a stopped container that is still the intended target.

proposal.reason: shop-db was stopped externally with a clean exit and nothing restarted it, so shop-web fails to resolve it. Starting it is allowed by the rules, and shop-web, shop-proxy and shop-worker should recover on their own once the database is back, so they are not restarted.

judge_reason: The diagnosis matches the expected cause: shop-db is stopped, preventing shop-web from connecting to the database and causing the API to fail. The clean shutdown and subsequent health-check and API failures provide consistent supporting evidence.

diagnosis.root_cause: shop-web runs shop version 2 (SHOP_VERSION, whose documented default is 1), and its /api/items reads the price_cents column added by commit 3350063 'Keep item prices in whole cents for shop 2'. The items table in shop-db never received migrations/0002_price_cents.sql, so every query fails with a missing-column error and returns 500. The code and the database schema do not match.

evidence.detail: shop-web logs show every GET /api/items failing in app.py line 90 because column price_cents does not exist. The container itself is healthy, since /health does not query items.
shop-db logs show the same missing price_cents error at 13:15:35 and 13:16:05, matching the two url_failed signals. The database is up and healthy.

Commit 3350063 'Keep item prices in whole cents for shop 2' makes SHOP_VERSION 2 read price_cents and adds migration 0002_price_cents.sql, which adds the column. Commit d9f9be1 'Deploy shop 2' followed (recent_commits).

deploy.md lists SHOP_VERSION for shop-web with default 1. services.md says shop-web only creates the items table on first start, with a price column, and the data outlives the container. No page describes applying migrations.
shop-web is running with 0 restarts and no OOM kill. Its environment was not fully visible, so SHOP_VERSION=2 is inferred from the query it runs. deployed_commits could not say which commit runs.

proposal.reason: shop-web runs shop 2, which reads a price_cents column that shop-db never received because migration 0002_price_cents.sql was not applied. Restarting any container would bring back the same error, and shop-db must not be stopped or restarted.
proposal.human_instructions: Choose one of two fixes. (1) Roll back: in demo/compose.yaml set SHOP_VERSION for shop-web back to its documented default of 1 (or remove the override), then run `docker compose up -d shop-web` to recreate it. (2) Roll forward: apply migrations/0002_price_cents.sql from commit 3350063 to the shop-db items table, for example `docker compose exec -T shop-db psql -U <db user> -d <db name> < migrations/0002_price_cents.sql`. Take a backup first, because the table holds the shop's items. Fill in the user and database name from your compose file, since I have not seen them. Do not restart shop-db. After either fix, check http://localhost:8080/api/items.

judge_reason: The diagnosis matches the expected root cause: shop-web version 2 queries price_cents, but shop-db lacks the column because its migration never ran, causing /api/items to return 500 while the web container remains healthy.

diagnosis.root_cause: shop-web's DATABASE_URL in demo/compose.yaml names the host 'db', which is no container or network alias; the database container is shop-db. The name fails to resolve at startup, so shop-web exits with code 3 and loops under restart policy unless-stopped. The docs give the host and port as shop-db:5432.

evidence.detail: Every shop-web start fails with a DNS error resolving host 'db', logs that it cannot reach the database, and exits during startup.
shop-web's DATABASE_URL points at host db on port 5432. OOMKilled is false, there is no memory limit, and the exit code is 3 with 8 restarts.
shop-db is running and healthy, pg_isready reports accepting connections, and it has 0 restarts. The database is up and only the name used to reach it is wrong.
Docs page demo/shop/docs/deploy.md (Settings) gives the DATABASE_URL default as the shop database on shop-db:5432, so the host should be shop-db.

proposal.reason: shop-web fails because DATABASE_URL in demo/compose.yaml uses host 'db' instead of 'shop-db'. Restarting it would only bring the same fault back, and Bleep cannot edit files or recreate containers.
proposal.human_instructions: In demo/compose.yaml, change shop-web's DATABASE_URL so the host is shop-db (shop-db:5432, as in demo/shop/docs/deploy.md) instead of db. Keep the rest of the URL as it is. Then apply it with `docker compose up -d shop-web` from the demo directory. Do not stop or restart shop-db.

judge_reason: The diagnosis matches the expected root cause: shop-web's DATABASE_URL uses the nonexistent host `db` instead of `shop-db`, so it cannot reach the database and exits at startup under the restart policy. The evidence that shop-db is healthy and the docs specify shop-db:5432 supports this conclusion.

diagnosis.root_cause: The `uploads` volume, a 20 MB in-memory (tmpfs) volume mounted at /uploads, is full. shop-web's /health check writes to it and fails with 'No space left on device', so shop-web reports unhealthy and returns 503 on /health.

evidence.detail: shop-web logged 'No space left on device' for uploads on every health check from 13:17:55. /health returned 503 while /api/items still returned 200, so the app and its database are up.

shop-web is running with 0 restarts and OOMKilled false. Its health probes went from exit 0 at 13:17:45 to HTTP 503 afterwards. The shop_uploads volume is mounted at /uploads, read-write in shop-web and read-only in shop-worker.

Repo docs deploy.md and services.md say the uploads volume is capped at 20 MB, is tmpfs, and keeps its files while a container that mounts it runs. This matches the volume filling up. The docs give no value for WORKER_BATCH_MB.
shop-web uses 66.8 MiB of 7.7 GiB memory and 0.3% CPU. The host is not short of memory or CPU, so the limit hit is the volume's own cap.
shop-worker reports 1 upload waiting from batch 3 onward, so a file is sitting in the uploads volume. Its 8 MB batches fit well inside its 64 MiB memory limit.

proposal.reason: The uploads tmpfs volume is full at its 20 MB cap, and a tmpfs volume keeps its files while any container that mounts it is running. Restarting shop-web alone would not clear it, because shop-worker still holds the volume, and clearing it by stopping and starting both needs four steps, over the three-step limit. It would also only delay the fault, since the cap and the waiting upload would still be there.
proposal.human_instructions: Free the uploads volume and fix what fills it. First look at what is in the shop_uploads volume, for example `docker exec shop-web ls -la /uploads`, and find the upload that shop-worker reports waiting since batch 3. Then change the shop's settings in demo/compose.yaml so the volume has room: raise the uploads tmpfs size above 20 MB, or reduce the worker's batch size (WORKER_BATCH_MB), and make sure the waiting upload gets consumed. The docs give no value for WORKER_BATCH_MB, so choose it yourself. Apply it with `docker compose up -d` from the demo directory. Recreating the containers that mount the volume will also empty it. Do not touch shop-db.

judge_reason: The diagnosis matches the expected root cause: the 20 MB uploads volume is full, causing shop-web writes to fail with “No space left on device” and its health check to fail. The evidence that /api/items still returns 200 and the container is not resource-starved supports the same cause rather than merely describing a symptom.

diagnosis.root_cause: shop-web is running, but its /health endpoint stopped answering within the 3 s probe timeout after the first probe passed at 13:19:01, so Docker marked it unhealthy. The cause of the hang is not established: shop-web's environment (SHOP_DEBUG_HOOK, DATABASE_URL) was not seen, and neither the database query nor the uploads write that /health performs was tested.

evidence.detail: shop-web's first probe at 13:19:01 passed. Every later probe timed out at 3 s. The container is running with restart count 0, OOMKilled false and no memory limit.
shop-web uses 0.0% CPU and 57 MiB of memory with 4 pids. That points to a request blocked on something, not a crash or resource exhaustion.
shop-web logged no error and no request after the hang began. Before it, /health and /api/items from 172.23.0.5 returned 200.
shop-db is healthy and logged only startup lines, with no errors or lock messages. shop-worker mounts /uploads read-only, logs a batch every 10 s and is not hitting its 64 MiB limit.

demo/shop/docs/services.md says /health queries the database and writes to the uploads volume. demo/shop/docs/deploy.md lists SHOP_DEBUG_HOOK, default 0, which enables debug routes. No doc ties either to a hang, and no setting value was collected.

judge_reason: The diagnosis matches the expected cause: shop-web remains running but hangs and stops answering requests, causing the health check to time out. Its evidence that later probes timed out and the container stayed running supports this; the evaluation does not require identifying what caused the hang.

diagnosis.root_cause: The running shop-proxy (Caddy) was hot-loaded at 13:21:01 through its admin API from /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.misroute, which sends upstream traffic to 172.23.0.4:8001. Nothing listens on 8001, because shop-web serves on port 8000, so every request gets a 502. The original /etc/caddy/Caddyfile worked until that load.

evidence.detail: shop-proxy served /health and /api/items normally after starting at 13:20:55 with /etc/caddy/Caddyfile. A POST /load from inside the container at 13:21:01 loaded /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.misroute, and the first 502 came at 13:21:31.
Every proxy error since then is a refused connection to 172.23.0.4:8001, the upstream address and port the loaded config uses.

shop-web listens on 0.0.0.0:8000, its health probes pass, and it has had no restarts or OOM kills. So the upstream port should be 8000, not 8001. This value comes from shop-web's own startup log; no docs were searched.

shop-proxy is running with restart count 0, no OOM kill and no memory limit. shop-db is healthy and shop-worker is processing batches, so the fault is in the proxy's routing and not in a crash or resource limit.
There were no Docker events in the last 30 minutes, so no container restart or recreate caused this. The config was swapped in the running proxy.

proposal.reason: The 502s began when Caddyfile.misroute (upstream port 8001) was hot-loaded into the running shop-proxy through its admin API. The file on disk, /etc/caddy/Caddyfile, is the one that worked at startup, so restarting the proxy should drop the runtime config and load the original one. shop-web, shop-db and shop-worker are healthy and need no action.

judge_reason: The diagnosis identifies the same root cause: shop-proxy routes requests to shop-web on port 8001, where nothing listens, while shop-web is healthy and listens on 8000. The evidence that the misrouted config was hot-loaded adds correct detail.

diagnosis.root_cause: shop-worker's batch size, set by the environment variable WORKER_BATCH_MB and logged as 256 MB, is far above the container's 64 MiB memory limit (no swap). It is OOM-killed (exit 137) after loading about 48 MB of each batch, and `unless-stopped` restarts it into the same crash. The docs give no value for WORKER_BATCH_MB, only that it must stay well under 64 MB. The setting lives in demo/compose.yaml.

evidence.detail: shop-worker has OOMKilled true, exit code 137, a 64 MiB memory limit and restart policy unless-stopped. It has restarted 8 times. WORKER_BATCH_MB is in its env, with the value hidden.
Each shop-worker start logs a batch size of 256 MB, loads 16, 32 and 48 MB, then dies before reaching the 64 MiB limit. This repeats on every restart.
deploy.md (Limits and restarts) says shop-worker is limited to 64 MB of memory with no swap, and that demo/compose.yaml is the only place settings live.
Four searches of the repo docs, including one for WORKER_BATCH_MB by name, found no page that gives a value or sizing rule for it, so the docs give none.
shop-db, shop-web and shop-proxy are running and healthy where checked. Host memory is 7.7 GiB in total, so the failure is confined to shop-worker's own limit.

proposal.reason: shop-worker is OOM-killed because WORKER_BATCH_MB (256 MB) is far above its 64 MiB memory limit, so a restart would only bring the same crash back. The setting is in demo/compose.yaml, which Bleep cannot edit or apply with docker compose.
proposal.human_instructions: Edit demo/compose.yaml and lower WORKER_BATCH_MB for shop-worker to a value well under the 64 MB memory limit (the docs give no exact value, so choose one with real headroom, for example a fraction of 64). Then apply it with: docker compose up -d shop-worker. Do not touch shop-db. After that, check http://localhost:8080/health and http://localhost:8080/api/items.

judge_reason: The diagnosis matches the expected cause: shop-worker has WORKER_BATCH_MB set to 256, exceeding its 64 MB memory limit, so it is OOM-killed and repeatedly restarts. The extra evidence is consistent with that cause.

diagnosis.root_cause: shop-proxy could not start because host port 8080 was already allocated: Docker failed to bind 0.0.0.0:8080 when the container was recreated, so it exited with code 128. Something else on demo is holding 8080 and answering the probes with a reply that lacks the expected text; I could not identify what it is.

evidence.detail: shop-proxy exited with code 128, OOMKilled false, restart count 0. The engine error says the bind for 0.0.0.0:8080 failed because the port is already allocated.
The url_failed probes on http://localhost:8080/api/items and /health got HTTP 200 in 5-7 ms without the expected text, so a different listener is answering on 8080.
shop-web is healthy and serves /health and /api/items with 200 OK, and shop-db and shop-worker are running, so the backend is fine and only the proxy in front is down.
No events in the last 240 minutes, so there is no record of what took port 8080 or when.

proposal.reason: shop-proxy is down because something else on demo already holds port 8080, and a plain restart would fail with the same bind error. Freeing the port and recreating the container are outside what Bleep can do, and I must not stop another workload to make room.
proposal.human_instructions: Find what is listening on port 8080 on demo (for example `docker ps --filter publish=8080` and `ss -ltnp 'sport = :8080'`). That listener is not shop-web, which is healthy and not the cause. Decide whether it may be stopped, or whether the shop's proxy port should change in demo/compose.yaml. Once 8080 is free (or the port is changed in demo/compose.yaml), recreate the proxy with `docker compose up -d --force-recreate shop-proxy`. Do not restart shop-db.

judge_reason: The diagnosis correctly identifies that shop-proxy cannot start because port 8080 is already allocated, and that another listener answers the shop URLs. However, it says the listener could not be identified instead of naming shop-canary, the expected process holding the port.
